purpose: Curated, location-aware scene families. Generic travel rooms share only approved art; landmarks keep their exact room art or a hand-curated override.

deep-forest.habitat: forested wilderness without a named landmark

desert.habitat: unnamed dunes, sands and desert roads

rejects: swamp renders dominated by cottages or unrelated buildings
mountain-pass renders that depict town streets and buildings

Crossing.subject: large working trade town and player hub
Crossing.terrain: lowland town with riverfront, gates, greens and dense commercial core
Crossing.builtForm: mixed timber and stone construction; practical streets, civic squares, guild compounds, market frontage and working quays
Crossing.atmosphere: busy, old, prosperous in places, rough in others; a town people actually work and live in rather than a pristine fantasy capital
generationHints: visible wear, carts, awnings, barrels and trade clutter only where room text supports them

town-green-civic.subject: Crossing civic heart and Town Green
visualLanguage: open civic space
grass or planted public ground where supported
busy surrounding town frontage
fountains, monuments or civic details only when named

market-commercial.subject: dense commercial Crossing
visualLanguage: close shopfronts and awnings
pedestrian trade traffic
goods, carts and signs only when supported
more visual clutter than residential streets

river-quays.subject: Crossing riverfront and working quays
visualLanguage: water must read clearly when the room supports it
working timber docks and stone embankments
rope, cargo and boats only where supported
do not reuse inland street compositions

gates-walls.subject: Crossing gates and defensive perimeter
visualLanguage: fortified town wall rather than giant castle
gate traffic and practical defenses
clear inside/outside orientation when supported

temple-quarter.subject: Crossing religious approaches and temple quarter
visualLanguage: quieter ceremonial streets
religious architecture only when room text establishes it
cleaner sightlines than market streets
do not invent glowing magic or cathedral scale

residential-backstreets.subject: Crossing lanes, courts and poorer backstreets
visualLanguage: narrower irregular routes
more enclosed framing
worn practical buildings
avoid turning every alley into a criminal slum

riverpine-outskirts.subject: greener Crossing outskirts around Riverpine
visualLanguage: settlement thins toward vegetation and open land
roads and trees become more important than shopfronts
use wilderness baskets when room semantics clearly leave town

guild-civic-interiors.subject: major Crossing institutions
visualLanguage: institution-specific interiors
Crossing materials can unify them but room function dominates
never substitute generic city-street art for interiors

amusement-carousel.subject: Crossing amusement and carousel complex
visualLanguage: distinct entertainment identity
color and ornament may be stronger than ordinary Crossing
must be generated or curated as a special family rather than generic streets

avoid: one generic medieval street representing the entire town
forcing river, temple, market or fortification details into unrelated rooms

Ratha.subject: fortified urban center
Ratha.builtForm: dark stone, defensive and disciplined architecture
